 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Meeting Compensation Disclosure
Pursuant to Government Code Section 54952.3: Disclosure of compensation for meeting
attendance by City Council Members is $790 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

Proclamations, Certificates, Introductions And Ceremonial Actions - NONE
Public Hearings - NONE
Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous

  2
 comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 1, 2, 3 and 4 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including Ordinances,
Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these
items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific items be
removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be

  7
 continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

PURPOSE:  To approve  the job  specifications  and salary  range  for the Recreation  Marketing
Coordinator  position  in the Parks and Recreation  Department,  update  the Accountant  position  in
the Administrative  Services  Department,  and update respective  salary ranges and salary pay tables.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  adopting  a Resolution  amending
Resolution  No. 6454 (Salary  Resolution  and Position  Classification  Plan) adding  a new Recreation
Marketing  Coordinator  classification  in the  Parks  and  Recreation  Department,  ripdating  the
Accountant  classification  in the Administrative  Services  Department,  approving  the corresponding
job specifications  and ripdating  the appropriate  salary pay tables.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The fiscal  impact  from  the Recreation  Marketing  Coordinator  position  will
be an additional  $3,696 per year.  The increase  of $3,696  represents  the difference  between  the
budgeted  position  and the proposed  position.  The Accountant  position  is fully  funded.

ANALYSIS:  None.

job  specifications  and/or  compensation  in the Salary  Resolution  and Position  Classification  Plan
in order to satisfy  the changing  needs and demands  of the workforce  and to more  closely  match
the tasks which  need to be performed  by employees  in the City's  various  departments.

An  Intermediate  Typist  Clerk  position  in the Parks  and Recreation  Department  was  recently
vacated.  Staff is recommending  replacing  this position  with  a Recreation  Marketing  Coordinator
position  to more  accurately  reflect  the functions  needed  and the duties  being  performed  in the
position.  The City  Council  has emphasized  the importance  of cornrnunication  between  employees

Gate.

The fornner Accountant  job specification  was updated.  This position  has not been active  in recent
years.  Staff is proposing  bringing  it back to address recruitment  challenges.  Currently,  there is a
vacantSeniorAccountantpositionthattheCityhasnotbeenabletofill.  Severalrecruitmentshave

SERVICES  FOR  THE  RAISING  CANE'S  DEVELOPMENT  LOCATED  AT  9854
ALAMEDA  AVENUE

PURPOSE:  The KOA  Corporation  provides  construction  monitoring  and inspection  services
through  Contract  No. 2022-59-AC  to oversee  public  improvements  required  to be constructed  for
the  Raising  Cane's  development  located  at 9854  Alameda  Avenue.  Parkway  Construction
Company,  the developer,  took 28 days longer  than originally  scheduled  to complete  construction.
Amendment  No. 1 is needed to fund 28 additional  working  days of services  provided  by KOA.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  l to Contract  No.  2022-59-AC  with  KOA  Corporation,  to
  fund construction  monitoring  and inspection  services  for an additional  28 working  days at
  the request  of the Parkway  Construction  Company,  the developer  of the Raising  Cane's
  development  located  at 9854 Alameda  Avenue,  for an amount  not to exceed  $30,000;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  l to Contract  No.  2022-59-AC  in a
  form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  Amendment  No.  1 to Contract
No.  2022-59-AC  is for  an amount  not  to exceed  $30,000.  It will  be funded  by the Parkway
Construction  Company.  The  City  has  collected  a total  deposit  of  $77,520  from  Parkway
Construction  Company  to pay for these services,  which  have been deposited  to Account  No. 100-
2258.

ANALYSIS:  The  Public  Works  Department,  Engineering  Division,  utilizes  the  services  of
professional  services  consultants  to meet the demand  for construction  monitoring  and inspection
services  from  private  development  that  require  a significant  amount  of construction  oversight

  1

  25
 beyond  the division's  staffing  capacity.  Currently,  KOA  Corporation  is under  contract  to provide
construction  monitoring  and inspection  services  for  the  offsite  improvements  required  to be
constructed  by the Raising  Cane's  development.  Contract  No.  2022-59-AC  funded  services  for
48 days as requested  by the Parkway  Construction  Company.  However,  the developer  extended
the  construction  schedule  by  28  working  days,  from  a total  of  48  to  76  working  days.
Accordingly,  Amendment  No.  1 is needed  to fund  the additional  28 working  days  of services
provided  by KOA  in the amount  not to exceed  $30,000.

BACKGROUND:  As  part  of  the  Design  Review  Case  No.  2021-001  the  Public  Works
Department  required  the  construction  of  offsite  improvements  for  the  Raising  Cane's
development.  This  included  but was not limited  to curb ramps,  sidewalk  repairs,  installation  of
new fire hydrant,  reconstructing  driveway  approaches  and planting  trees.

On August  9, 2022, the City  Manager  administratively  approved  Contract  No. 2022-59-AC  with
KOA  Corporation  to provide  construction  monitoring  and inspection  services  for a not-to-exceed
amount  of  $47,520. Services  entailed  providing  an inspector  to oversee  construction  of the
offsite  improvements,  on behalf  of the City.  The contract  was based on 48 working  days.

The  Parkway  Construction  Company  has requested  an additional  28 days  of  service  as the
construction  scheduled  was increased  from  48 to 76 total  working  days.  Parkway  Construction
Company  encountered  delays  from  installing  conduits  inconsistent  with  Southern  California
Edison's  specifications,  significant  amounts  of concrete  were required  to be replaced,  and a lack
of  efficient  scheduling  occurred  with  public  utilities.  These  delays  extended  construction
monitoring  services  by an additional  28 working  days. Construction  is not complete.

Amendment  No.  1 retroactively  extends  the term  of Contract  No.  2022-59-AC  from  September
30, 2022 to December  23, 2022 and increases  the amount  of Contract  No. 2022-59-AC  to a total
of $77,520.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is in the FY  2022/23  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP").  The
Project  is being  implemented  to improve  pedestrian  and vehicular  safety  and relieve  traffic  congestion
on Tweedy  Boulevard.  More  specifically,  the Project  will  synchronize  13 traffic  signals  along  Tweedy
Boulevard,  between  Victoria  Avenue  and Atlantic  Avenue.  This  entails  installing  conduit  and cabling
to physically  connect  the traffic  signals.  The proposed  improvements  include  the installation  of fiber
optic  cable,  upgrade  cabinets  and controllers,  re-wire  intersections  and install  video  detection  systems.
The design  phase is complete  and the Project  is ready to begin  construction.

On October  27, 2022,  staff  advertised  the Notice  Inviting  Bids  for construction  in the Daily  Journal.
The Project  was also advertised  on the City's  website  and Ebidboard.  On November  17, 2022, the City
held a bid opening  at the City  Clerk's  Office.  Five (5) bids were received,  as summarized  below.

  No.  Contactor  Base Bid  Amount

  California  Professional  Engineering,  Inc.  $1,833,198
  Select Electric,  Inc.  $2,151,287
  Belco  Elecnor  $2,224,134
  DBX,  Inc.  $2,318,025
  Baker  Electric  & Renewables,  LLC  $8,145,193

California  Professional  Engineering,  Inc.  submitted  the lowest  responsible  and responsive  bid.  Its bid
was reasonably  close to the engineer's  estimate  of $1,800,000.

California  Professional  Engineering,  Inc., is based in the City  of La Puente.  The company  has been in
business  for over twenty  years and has the experience  to construct  the Project.

Pursuant  to  the  guidelines  of  the  California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  this  Project  is
categorically  exempt  under  Title  14 of the California  Code  of Regulations,  Section  15301,  Class  1
(Existing  Facilities)  provides  for  an exemption  for  operation,  maintenance  and  repair  of  existing
infrastructure,  which  will  be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Clerk/Registrar-Recorder.

Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in March  2023 and is scheduled  to be completed  in August  2023.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  GREEN  GIANT  LANDSCAPE,  INC.,  FOR  THE
CONSTRUCTION  OF  ELECTRIC  VEHICLE  CHARGING  STATIONS,  CITY
PROJECT  NO.  636-GEN

PURPOSE:  To award  an agreement  to Green  Giant  Landscape,  Inc.,  for the construction  of
the Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations  Project.  The project  is a part of the Capital  Improvement
Program.  Design  is complete  and the project  is ready  for construction.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  Green  Giant  Landscape,  Inc.,  for the construction  of the
  Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations,  City  Project  No.  636-GEN  ("Project"),  in an amount
  not-to-exceed  $267,734;

  b. Appropriating  $142,969 from  the AQMD  Fund  Balance,  $60,000 in Mobile  Source  Air
  Pollution  Reduction  Review  Committee  ("MSRC")  Grant  Funds  and $75,000  in Water
  Funds to Account  No. 311-790-49-9914  to fully  fund the Project;

  c.  Approving  the deobligation  of the $60,000 in Measure  M funds  from  the Project  which
  funds  did  not  qualify  for  use  for  the  construction  of  the  Electric  Vehicle  Charging
  Stations,  City  Project  No. 636-GEN;

  d.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to administratively  approve  change  orders  for  agreement,
  not to exceed the aggregate  sum of $75,000;
  e.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney;  and

  f.  Adopting  a finding  determining  the  Electric  Vehicle  Charging  Stations  Project  as
  categorically  exempt  under  Title  14 of the Code  of Regulations  under  Existing  Facilities,
  Section  15301  Class  l(b);  and

  g.  Approving  the Notice  of Exemption  for the construction  of the Project  and directing  the
  City  Clerk  to file it with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement
with  Green  Giant  Landscape,  Inc.  will  be 'Junded  as summarized  on the following  page.  The
proposed  appropriations  are $142,969 in AQMD  Funds,  $60,000  in MSRC  Grant  Funds  and

ANALYSIS:  The proposed  contract  was procured  through  a competitive  bid  process.  Green
Giant  Landscape,  Inc.,  submitted  the only  bid.  Staff  is recommending  proceeding  to award  a
construction  contract  in the amount  of $267,734.

To  date,  the  City  Council  has appropriated  $251,709  to the project  inclusive  of  $77,400  in
MSRC  Grant  funds,  $114,309  in  AQMD  Funds  and  $60,000  in  Measure  M  Funds.
Appropriations  are needed  to re-establish  this  budgetary  level  as well  as to provide  additional
funding  to fully  fund construction,  as follows:

  *  Appropriation  of  $60,000  in  MSRC  Grant  Funds:  The  appropriation  is needed  to
  establish  that the full  amount  of the $77,400  grant  is available  for the project,  as only
  $17,400  was carried  over to the current  year CIP during  the annual  budgeting  process.

  *  Appropriation  of $142,969  in AQMD  Funds:  The $60,000  Measure  M Funds  previously
  approved  were not an allowable  approval  for the project.  The appropriation  is needed to
  replace  the funds  with  $60,000  in AQMD  Funds  as well  as to provide  $82,969  to further
  fund the project.

  *  Appropriation  of $75,000  in Water  Funds:  An  appropriation  is recommended  to 'fund
  construction  and related  services  for  one of the two  electric  vehicle  charging  stations
  proposed  at the Public  Works  Department,  Field  Operations  Corporate  Yard.

The total  funding  proposed  to be added  above  the $251,709  budgetary  level  is $157,969,  for a
total proposed  budget  of $409,678.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is part of the City's  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The Project
entails  installing  five electrical  vehicle  charging  stations  located  at City  Hall  Parking  Garage  (l-
Dual  charging  station),  Police  Department  (2-Dual  charging  Stations),  and at the Public  Works
Corporate  Yard  (2-Dual  charging  Stations).  The  Project  also includes  the installation  of new
panels,  electrical  conduit  and  conductors,  switches,  breakers,  hardware,  concrete  pads,  and
construction  of an ADA  ramp.

For budgetary  reasons,  the project  was bid  with  a Base Bid,  Additive  Alternate  Bid  and three
Deductive  Alternates.  The Base Bid  included  the aforementioned  improvements.  The Additive
Alternate  Bid  included  an additional  dual  charging  station  at the Civic  Center.  The Deductive

  2

   Bids  included  removing  one EV  charging  stations  from  the Police  Station,  Field  Operations
  Corporate  Yard  and City  Hall  garage.  This  bid  strategy  was utilized  to provide  flexibility  in
  awarding  a contract  since  construction  bids  have  come  in high  as compared  to the engineers
  estimates  and budgetary  amounts  on various  projects.

  On October  27, 2022,  staff  re-advertised  the Notice  Inviting  Bids  for construction  in the Daily
  Journal.  The Project  was also advertised  on the City's  website  and Ebidboard.  On November  28,
  2022,  one bid was received  and opened  by the City  Clerk  in a public  forum.  The summary  of the
  bid is as follows:

  Staff  is recommending  awarding  the Base Bid  and the Additive  Alternate  Bid  in the amount  of
  $267,734 to construct  EV  Charing  Stations  at the City  Hall  Parking  Garage  (l-Dual  charging
  station),  Police  Department  (2-Dual  charging  Stations),  Public  Works  Corporate  Yard  (2-Dual
  charging  Stations)  and the Civic  Center  (l-Dual  charging  station).

  Green  Giant  Landscape,  Inc., is based in La Habra,  California.  It has been in business  for over 26
  years.  Staff  contacted  listed  references  and received  positive  commentary.  The company  has the
  capacity  and experience  to perform  the work  required  under the bid solicitation.

  On September  20, 2022,  staff  received  a formal  letter  indicating  that the City  can use a non-
  certified  installer  for the EV charging  stations  without  voiding  the warranty.

  The City  Council  will  authorize  the City  Manager  to administratively  approve  change  orders  up
  to $75,000.  This  will  accelerate  project  changes  to avoid  delays  in payment  or delays  in the
  construction  schedule.

  Pursuant  to the guidelines  of the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  this Project  is
  categorically  exempt  under  Title  14 of the California  Code of Regulations,  Section  15301,  Class
  1(b) exemption  for replacement  for public  utility  services.

  The proposed  EV Charging  Stations  will  require  software  provided  by Zevtron,  LLC.,  to manage
  and track the energy consumption  at each station,  at a cost of $9,000, under  a separate  software
  service  agreement.  The Zevtron  software  is customizable  to meet the City's  needs. The so:[tware
  allows  the  City  to  control  and  manage  the  consumption  of  energy  through  a cloud-based
  management  platform.  If desired,  prices  can be set for each charging  station  as well  as notify
  users when vehicles  are fully  charged.  The software  can limit  who uses the chargers  and for how
  long.  Status and reporting  is available  any time.

  Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in March  2023.  The procurement  lead time  is estimated  to be
  20 weeks.  It is anticipated  that the Project  will  be completed  in October  2023.

SUBJECT:  CITY  COUNCIL  APPOINTMENTS  TO  THE  VARIOUS  CITY
COMMISSIONS,  COMMITTEES  AND  BOARDS

PURPOSE:  Under  the  South  Gate  Municipal  Code,  City  Council  Members  are permitted  to
nominate  individual  or  individuals  to  various  City  Commissions  or  Boards  subject  to  the
ratification  of the City  Council.  This  agenda item  contains  several  nominations  by City  Council
Members  to fill  vacancies  on these Commissions  and Boards.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Ratifying  the nomination  by City  Council  Member  Al Rios  of Mr.  Jimmy  Ozaeta  to the
  Plaru"iing  Commission;
  b.  Ratifying  the nomination  by City  Council  Member  Al  Rios  of Mr.  Edgar  Pelayo  to the
  Parks and Recreation  Commission;  and
  c.  Ratifying  the nomination  by Vice  Mayor  Gil  Hurtado  of Ms.  Jovanna  Laborin  to the
  Planning  Commission

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

ANALYSIS:  These appointments  would  be effective  Januaiy  11, 2023,  if approved  by the City
Council.  The appointments  must be ratified  by a majority  vote of the City  Council.

Mr.  Jimmy  Ozaeta  is a 34-year  resident  of South  Gate, attended  local  South  Gate schools  and is
currently  the Chief  Advance  Officer  for UMMA  Community  Clinic  in Los Angeles.

Mr.  Edgar  Pelayo  is a 35-year  resident  of South  Gate  and a business  consultant  that believes
strongly  in leisure  services.

Ms. Jovanna  Laborin  is a 45-year  resident  of South  Gate and is active  in many  activities  within
the community.

BACKGROUND:  In accordance  with  the MADDY  Act,  the City  posted  the opening  of the
positions  and  accepted  applications  from  the  public  for  the  required  20  days  prior  to
appointment,  Due to the recent  elections,  all appointments  for the effective  elected  offices  are
considered  ended when  the new term begins  pursuant  to the South  Gate Municipal  Code.  In this
case, the effective  offices  are those of Council  Members  Joshua Barron  and Al Rios.  Individuals

SUBJECT:  DISCUSSION  ON WHETHER  THE  CITIZENS'  ADVISORY  COMMITTEE
MEMBERSHIP  SIZE  SHOULD  BE CHANGED

PURPOSE:  To allow  the City  Council  to discuss  and give direction  to staff on whether  to prepare
an Ordinance  that would  alter  the size of the Citizens'  Advisory  Committee  ("CAC")  from  its
current  size of 20 members.  This  item  was requested  by Mayor  Avalos  and former  Council
Member  Diaz  in January  2022.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Directing  staff  to prepare  an ordinance  that  would  amend  the size of the Citizens'
  Advisory  Committee  from  the current  membership  level  of 20 members  to a lower
  membership  number;  or
  b.  Maintaining  the current  membership  size.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

BACKGROUND:  The  Housing  and Urban  Development  Department  ("HUD")  requires  that
entitlement  cities  adopt  a citizen's  participation  plan  to provide  opportunities  for  community
involvement  in  the  planning,  development,  implementation,  monitoring  and  evaluation  of
Community  Development  Block  Grant  ("CDBG")  funded  programs.

The City  usually  receives  its annual  notice  of funding  allocation  for CDBG  and HOME  funds  in
the last quarter  of the fiscal  year (April-June),  but that can be delayed  if Congress  does not pass a
HUD  budget  bill  in a timely  manner.  Regardless  of the delay,  the City  is required  to submit  its
Aru'iual  Action  Plan by the 15I'1 of May,  unless extended  by Congressional  action.

The  CAC  was established  to provide  the City  Council  with  recornrnendations  on how  to best
distribute  CDBG  funds.  The CAC  is unique  in that it currently  consists  of 20 members  that may
be required  to meet up to six (6) times  between  the months  of January  and April.  However,  due to
the inconsistency  in meeting  schedule,  many  of the cornrnittee  members  have had a difficult  time
attending  meetings.  More  importantly,  pursuant  to the Brown  Act,  11 committee  members  (50%
plus  one)  must  be present  at each meeting  to have  a quorum,  or the meeting  will  have  to be

  1

  122
 rescheduled.  Finding  alternative  dates  not  only  adds  pressure  to the  members,  due  to prior
commitments,  but it has also been difficult  to find  a date that works  for at least 11 members.

The City's  other  Commissions  and Boards  are made up of five  members  with  each City  Council
member  having  nominated  one member.  These bodies  meet once or twice  a month  at a regularly
scheduled  day and time  in the City  Council  Chambers.  These set times  allow  the members  of the
Commission  or Board  to plan in advance,  therefore  problems  with  attendance  are minimal.

ANALYSIS:  The City,  as an entitlement  city, receives  CDBG  and HOME  Investment  Partnerships
Program  (HOME)  funds annually  from HUD  to carry out a wide range of community  development
activities  which  benefit  low-income  residents.

The City's  adopted  Citizen's  Participation  Plan, which  is a component  of the Consolidated  Plan,
defines  that the CAC  has been established  to assist the City  Council  in making  fiinding  decisions
related  to CDBG  Programs.  Each  City  Council  member  nominates  four  (4)  members  to the
Committee  and  each  Committee  member  serves  at the  pleasure  of  their  appointing  City
Councilmember  during  their  respective  term.  The  term  of  office  of  any  cornrnittee  member
automatically  expires  if the committee  member  is absent  from  three  (3) consecutive  regularly
scheduled  meetings  without  notice  to the CDBG  coordinator.

Entitlement  cities are required  to develop  an Annual  Action  Plan. Each year, the City will  send out
a Notice  of Funding  Availability  (NOFA)  to non-profit  agencies  and city  departments  advising
them  that the planning  cycle  has begun  for CDBG  :tunds, and that the City  is accepting  project
proposals  to provide  public  services  to qualifying  populations  or census tracts.  City  staff conducts
an eligibility  analysis  on all project  proposals  submitted  and reviews  the eligible  proposals  for
service  provider  funding  consideration.  The CAC  also reviews  the project  proposals  and makes
funding  recommendations  that are considered  by the City  Council  when they consider  the Annual
Action  Plan.  The Annual  Action  Plan must be submitted  to HUD  by May  15 of each year.

Based on the previous  occurrence  of CAC  meetings  being  cancelled  due to a lack of quorum,  then
Vice  Mayor  Avalos  and former  Council  Member  Diaz previously  suggested  that the City  Council
discuss  whether  the size of the CAC  should  be reduced  to a level  similar  to other Commissions  or
Boards  which  also serve to advise  the City  Council  on governmental  issues or concerns.

Staff  is recommending  that the City  Council  consider  lowering  the number  of members  of the
Citizens'  Advisory  Committee  down  to  10  members,  which  would  continue  to  allow  for
nominations  of a diverse  representation.  Decreasing  the size of the CAC  would  consequently  lower
the required  number  of committee  members  to reach a quorum  and thus, increasing  the chances  of
holding  a meeting  at its scheduled  time.

Currently,  two  Council  Members  have not nominated  any of their  four  representatives,  so this
change  to less members  may also be a more  opportunistic  time  to fill  these vacancies.  It would
also mean a less disruptive  process  to any existing  incumbents,  should  the City  Council  agree to
reduce the size of the Committee.

CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA

I  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2023
  CALL TO ORDER  Maria del Pilar Avalos, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to
  order at 6:45 p.m.

  INVOCATION  Bobby Scott, Community of Faith Bible Church

  PLEDGE OF
  ALLEGIANCE  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources

  ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

  PRESENT  Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Vice Mayor Gil Hurtado, Council Member
  Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria Davila, and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Chris Jeffers, City
  Attorney Raul F. Salinas

  CERTIFICATE  The City Council presented Pastor Bruszer a certificate in honor of his
  retirement.

  COMMENTS FROM

I  THE AUDIENCE  Sophie Ryan, South Gate Resident spoke on the Centennial Celebration.
  She suggested inviting Mr. Carvalho and Jackie Goldberg from LAUSD.

  Albert Castillo, Community Organizer for TreePeople spoke on receiving
  a grant in partnership with the City of South Gate to plant 1,300 trees and
  give away 1,000 fruit trees.

  Thomas Buckley asked Mr. Costley where the fireworks will be at the
  Centennial Celebration and asked Chief Arakawa for an update on a
  possible explosion earlier in the day. He also reported several locations
  that have street light outages and expressed his concerns over the new
  trash company. Finally, he would like Council to reinstate the 5-minute
  public comment period.

  Angel Colon congratulated the newly elected officials and spoke about
  Laverne Bates and her work with the city.

  Vanessa C. provided an update on the activities of Congresswomen
  Barragan.

  Mario Dominguez expressed his concerns with the 5-minute public

I  comment period, lack of cameras in the City Council Chambers and the
  Council voting to approve an increase in the salaries.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 10, 2023

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS Chief Arakawa responded that the explosion this afternoon was due to a
  juvenile igniting a firework.

  Kristopher Ryan, Director of Finance stated that the city is currently
  putting together the mid-year report for Council and update on the
  completed annual audit.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources stated that HR is currently
  reviewing systems and looking for ways to become a more efficient
  customer service-based department.

  Darren Arakawa, Chief of Police stated that the Police Department along
  with the Fire Department is hosting a CERT Class (Community
  Emergency Response Team). Members of the community will learn about
  fire safety, light weight search and rescue, and the class will be held in
  Spanish.

  Chief Arakawa reported on a Community Meeting held at the park.
  Members of UWS were there to talk about the trash hauler contract and
  parking concerns.

  Art Cervantes, Director of Public Works provided an update on the
  residential resurfacing project.

  Steve Costley, Director of Parks and Recreation provided an update
  regrowing portion of the greenspace at South Gate Park and Hollydale
  Regional Park.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk stated that she attended the South Gate Police
  Department and UWS meet up this last Saturday, and the Raising Cane
  opening.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer spoke about the UWS Collection Services
  and stated that he was in support of upgrading the technology in the
  Council Chambers.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager reminded everyone that the Homeless Count
  will be on January 25th, and we are looking for volunteers. He spoke
  about the transition of over 24,000 customers to the new refuse hauler. He
  thanked Mr. Cervantes and Isaac Bravo of the Public Works Department
  for their hard work over this transition period.

  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney discussed two new laws that came into
  effect as of January 1St (AB2449 and SB1100).

  Page 2 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 10, 2023

  REPORTS AND COMMENTS

I  FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  CONT'D  Council Member Davila attended the UWS Community Meeting, the
  Neighborhood Watch Meeting, and the opening of Raising Cane. She
  thanked the Chamber of Commerce for their work on the Christmas
  Parade and the Police Department and Compatior for their work during
  Christmas providing toys for the children of South Gate.

  Council Member Barron thanked Chief Arakawa for providing
  information on SEACCA and our residents' concerns. Council Member
  Barron attended the UWS Community Meeting and the grand opening of
  Raising Cane.

  Council Member Rios spoke on the UWS transition and thanked the
  Police Department for their work during Christmas providing toys for the
  children of South Gate. Council Member Rios informed the public that
  open enrollment for East Los Angeles College will be on January 21,
  2023.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado will be meeting with Congresswoman Barragan and
  one of the items of discussion will be available funding for streetlights.
  The Vice Mayor attended the grand opening of Raising Cane and the
  Neighborhood Watch Meeting. He also discussed the transition with

I  UWS and urged drivers to be careful with the heavy rains.

  Lastly, residents have been asking him about the price of natural gas and
  requested a report on this issue.

  Mayor Avalos encouraged residents to reach out to UWS so their concerns
  can be addressed. The mayor attended Raising Cane grand opening, the
  Christmas Parade and Police Navidad. Mayor Avalos stated that it came
  to her attention the residents, business owners and city staff had concerns
  with her becoming Mayor. She is here to serve the residents and
  encouraged everyone to reach out to her because her door is always open.

  CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 1, 2, 3 and 4 were approved by motion of Vice Mayor
  Hurtado and seconded by Council Member Barron. Council Member
  Davila recused herself from Item 3.

  Roll Call: Council Member Davila, yes (recused on Item 3); Council
  Member Barron, yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado,
  yes; Mayor Avalos, yes.

I
  Page 3 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 10, 2023

1
PERSONNEL  The City Council unanimously approved Resolution No. 2023-01-CC
  entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of south Gate,
  California, amending Resolution No. 6454 (Salary Resolution and Position
  Classification Plan) adding a new Recreation Marketing Coordinator
  classification in the Parks and Recreation Department, updating
  the Accountant classification in the Administrative Services Department,
  approving the corresponding job specifications and updating the
  appropriate salary pay tables during Consent Calendar.

2
PROPERTY USE  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar.

  a. Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. 2022-59-AC with KOA
  Corporation, to fund construction monitoring and inspection services
  for an additional 28 working days at the request of the Parkway
  Construction Company, the developer of the Raising Cane's
  development located at 9854 Alameda Avenue, for an amount not to
  exceed $30,000; and

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 1 to Contract No.
  2022-59-AC in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.
3
PARKING  The City Council approved items A, B, and C during Consent Calendar.
  Council Member Davila was recused from voting on this item.

  a. Contract No. 2023-01-CC with California Professional Engineering,
  Inc. ("Agreement"), for the construction of Tweedy Boulevard Signal
  Synchronization Project, LAMTA ID F7309, City Project No. 514-
  TRF ("Project"), in the amount not-to-exceed $1,833,198;

  b. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney; and

  c. Adopted a finding determining the Tweedy Boulevard Signal
  Synchronization Project as categorically exempt under Title 14 of the
  California Code of Regulations, Section 15301 and the projects are
  categorically exempt under Existing Facilities Section 15301 Class (c)
  Existing highways and streets, sidewalks, gutters, bicycle and
  pedestrian trails, and similar facilities (including road grading for the
  purpose of public safety) and to be categorically excluded under
  Section 326 of amended Chapter 3 of Title 23, United States Code (23
  U.S.C. § 326) without significant impacts on the environment as
  defined by the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).

  Page 4 of 8
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 10, 2023

  4

I  ENERGY PROGRAMS  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C, D, E, F, and G
  during Consent Calendar.

  a. Contract No. 2023-02-CC with Green Giant Landscape, Inc., for the
  construction of the Electric Vehicle Charging Stations, City Project
  No. 636-GEN ("Project"), in an amount not-to-exceed $267,734;

  b. Appropriated $142,969 from the AQMD Fund Balance, $60,000 in
  Mobile Source Air Pollution Reduction Review Committee ("MSRC")
  Grant Funds and $75,000 in Water Funds to Account No. 311-790-49-
  9914 to fully fund the Project;

  c. The deobligation of the $60,000 in Measure M funds from the Project
  which funds did not qualify for use for the construction of the Electric
  Vehicle Charging Stations, City Project No. 636-GEN;

  d. Authorized the City Manager to administratively approve change
  orders for agreement, not to exceed the aggregate sum of $75,000;

  e. Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney; and

I  f. Adopted a finding determining the Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
  Project as categorically exempt under Title 14 of the Code of
  Regulations under Existing Facilities, Section 15301 Class 1(b); and

  g. The Notice of Exemption for the construction of the Project and
  directing the City Clerk to file it with the Los Angeles County
  Registrar Recorder's Office.

  DEVIATE FROM
  THE AGENDA  At this time, there being no objections, Mayor Avalos stated that item 7
